solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Poor district to reach touring Hungary

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the reach phrase wraps around the country letter

parts.note: to reach a place is to get to it
H is the international vehicle code for Hungary

explanation.surface: Someone sets off to reach a poor district while on a tour of Hungary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts GET TO around H.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a slum or deprived quarter of a city, originally a segregated Jewish quarter.

clue.text: Creature with urge to break into short laugh

indicators.note: to break into means to force a way inside, so the urge word sits within the laugh

parts.note: a brief laugh is a single 'ha'
a yen is a longing or urge

explanation.surface: An animal with an urge to interrupt with a brief laugh, fittingly for one famed for laughing.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a doglike African scavenger, a kind of animal.

clue.text: Time to study philosopher is drudgery

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
John Stuart Mill was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: Spending time studying a philosopher is a dreary chore.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: monotonous repetitive work, like walking an endless belt or mill wheel.

clue.text: Admitting drinking, losing head

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the drinking word is dropped

parts.note: downing a pint is drinking it

explanation.surface: A drunk confessing to drinking, and losing their head over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' removes D from DOWNING.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to own up is to confess or acknowledge something.

clue.text: Be more steady at sea, lacking interest

definitions.meaning: a ship that leans over less to one side is steadier, read as two words

explanation.surface: A seasick passenger, keener for the ship to steady, loses all interest in anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: To list is to lean at sea, so the answer split as two words says 'list less', i.e. lean less.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: languid, without energy or enthusiasm for anything.

clue.text: Where one may train — Penny Lane perhaps

definitions.meaning: a London railway terminus, a place to catch a train, with 'train' posing as a verb for practising
Penny Lane is a road in the Merseyside city, made famous by a Beatles song

explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like practising; it means travelling by train. Penny Lane is a thoroughfare in the Beatles' home city.
explanation.definitionFit: A London mainline station, and literally a road in the Merseyside city of which Penny Lane is an example.

clue.text: Fellows move slowly in race over rough terrain

parts.note: the SCR, Senior Common Room, is where college fellows gather
to amble is to walk at a leisurely pace

explanation.surface: College dons stroll slowly in a cross-country race.
explanation.walkthrough: SCR is the Senior Common Room of an Oxford or Cambridge college, standing for its fellows.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcycle scramble is a race across rough, hilly ground.

clue.text: Left Arabian port bearing burden

parts.note: Aden is a port in Yemen on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A ship left an Arabian port carrying a heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: weighed down, carrying a load.

clue.text: Chap aiming for game and most tricks securing rubber finally in bridge

indicators.note: in places the assembled middle inside the bridge word

parts.note: a span is a bridge or arch

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the rearranged letters hold the final letter
tricks as a verb means plays tricks on, so the letters of most are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of rubber

explanation.surface: Bridge players chasing the game, most tricks and the rubber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricks' looks like a bridge term but signals the anagram, giving OTSM; 'bridge' too is not the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunter or shooter is a man who goes after game birds and animals.

clue.text: Easy terms French author used in 'Snow on Glacier River'

indicators.note: used in means the author's name is placed within the snow-and-river letters

parts.note: névé is granular snow on the upper part of a glacier
Jules Verne was a French novelist

explanation.surface: Reads like a book title by a French author, set on a snowy glacier river.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for hire purchase, buying on credit by instalments.

clue.text: Doctor with hospital procedure for delivery

parts.note: an op is a surgical operation

explanation.surface: A doctor carries out a hospital procedure to deliver a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' suggests childbirth; it means a drop, as in goods dropped off.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a drop-off of goods or supplies, e.g. an airdrop.

clue.text: He brought traveller's tale of standard dish from Turkey

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
doner kebab is a Turkish dish of spit-roasted meat

explanation.surface: A traveller brought a tale of a typical dish from Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: Chaucer's pilgrims each tell a tale on the road to Canterbury; one is a seller of indulgences.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: a seller of indulgences is one of Chaucer's Canterbury pilgrims, each of whom tells a tale.

clue.text: Keep quiet about trendy record

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the quiet word goes round the trendy word

parts.note: to mute is to silence or keep quiet
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stay silent about a fashionable music release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' looks like a noun for a disc; it is a verb, to note down.
explanation.definitionFit: To minute a meeting is to record it in its official notes; a verb.

clue.text: Gathered in trug, light fruit

indicators.note: gathered in means held within the words, so the letters run across trug and light

explanation.surface: Fruit picked into a light garden basket.
explanation.walkthrough: A trug is a shallow wooden garden basket.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a Jamaican citrus fruit, a cross of grapefruit and tangerine.

clue.text: One denying profits to philosopher

parts.note: gains are profits
A. J. Ayer was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: Someone who refuses to grant a philosopher any profits.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to deny or contradict, so one who does so is a contradicter.

clue.text: Prompt Archer to collect lady's case — it remains to be seen

indicators.note: to collect means to take in, so the punctual phrase gathers the lady letters

parts.note: prompt means punctual, arriving on schedule

indicators.note: case means the outer shell, the first and last letters of lady

parts.note: William Tell is the legendary Swiss archer, shortened to Will

explanation.surface: A punctual archer picks up a lady's suitcase, with the outcome still uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: The archer is the Swiss hero William Tell, shortened here to Will.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: we shall find out in due course; the future outcome is not yet known.

clue.text: Highly-armed irregular lent cadet

indicators.note: irregular means not in order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An irregular soldier lent to a cadet unit is heavily armed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly-armed' sounds military; it means having many arms like an octopus.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: an octopus or squid with many limbs is literally well armed.

clue.text: A printer working in temporary building

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A printer is at work inside a prefab.
explanation.walkthrough: Terrapin is a British brand of prefabricated classroom or office building.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade name for a prefabricated hut used as a temporary classroom or office in Britain.

clue.text: See 15
Organised students keep Northern women in order

indicators.note: keep means hold inside, so the students' union surrounds the northern letter

parts.note: the NUS is the National Union of Students, an organisation of students

explanation.surface: A students' union keeps northern women in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep' puts NUS around N; 'in order' means in a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: Women belonging to a religious order are sisters living under vows.

clue.text: Pull serving girl without resistance

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the girl word encloses the resistance letter

parts.note: a wench was a serving maid
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone tugs at a serving girl who offers no resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside, putting WENCH around R.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to twist or tug something sharply.

clue.text: I'm high-flying Brit in meteorological line

indicators.note: in places the British letter within the high-flying phrase

parts.note: I'm high-flying is rendered as I soar
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A high-flying British pilot boasts while crossing a weather front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts B inside I SOAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A line on a weather map joining points of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Dress up grand arty broadcaster

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the dress word is read bottom to top

parts.note: garb is dress or clothing
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A broadcaster dresses up grandly in arty clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses GARB. Melvyn Bragg presented the long-running South Bank Show on British arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Melvyn Bragg is a British broadcaster famous for arts programmes.

clue.text: Nymph in mountain — one features in The Ring

indicators.note: in places the nymph inside the mountain word

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or peak
an oread is a mountain nymph in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A nymph in a mountain, with someone appearing in Wagner's Ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Ring' suggests Wagner's opera cycle; it is the bullring.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfighter is a performer in the bullring.

clue.text: Wild animal — one of several in pound

definitions.meaning: the snow leopard of central Asia
a unit of weight, sixteen of which make a pound

explanation.definitionFit: A snow leopard of the Himalayas, and an imperial weight one sixteenth of a pound.

clue.text: Mimic returned some money

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: any means some, as in 'have you any?'
M is the economists' abbreviation for money, as in M1

explanation.surface: A copycat gave back a little cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns ANY + M around.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: an Asian starling famous for imitating human speech, so a mimic.

clue.text: Oil producer before home country

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
England is one of the Home Countries of the UK

explanation.surface: An oil producer predating the home country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil producer' suggests a petroleum state; it is a bird's oil gland.
explanation.definitionFit: A gland at a bird's tail that secretes the oil used in grooming feathers.

clue.text: Trawl collects ordinary fish

indicators.note: collects means gathers in, so the net word takes in the ordinary letter

parts.note: a dragnet is a net dragged along the sea bottom
O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: A trawl net brings in an ordinary fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collects' puts O inside DRAGNET.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a small brightly coloured spiny sea fish.

clue.text: Cautious financier has hour to cover margin

indicators.note: to cover means to surround, so the hour letters enclose the margin word

parts.note: an edge is a margin or border

explanation.surface: A careful investor has an hour to cover the margin on a trade.
explanation.definitionFit: One who hedges bets offsets risk by taking counterbalancing positions.
